audit_findings.title: Post-merger shares are paired with only a partial year of Ansys earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 30.0 million merger shares, 14.2% of the 211.808646 million-share denominator; missing pre-acquisition Ansys OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-merger shares reduce per-share value while anchor OE includes Ansys only from July 17, 2025.
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements include the financial results of Ansys prospectively from the Acquisition Date.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated numerator-denominator timing mismatch. The full equity claim is counted, but less than four months of Ansys earnings enter FY2025 OE. The MIN anchor rule makes the result conservative but does not make the numerator economically coextensive with the shares. A 14.2% merger-share component is large enough to affect intrinsic value materially.
audit_findings.action: Treat the valuation as provisional and rerun it using the first full-year combined 10-K, with full-year combined OE and the contemporaneous diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: The ten-year growth record may cross a divestiture perimeter break
audit_findings.magnitude: Software Integrity revenue was $524.605 million in FY2023 and $468.720 million in FY2024; its effect on 2016-2024 OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent continuing-operations perimeters can distort the historical OE trend and any growth assumptions informed by that trend.
audit_findings.evidence: The financial results of the Software Integrity business are presented as income from discontinued operations, net of income taxes in our consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: The divestiture and discontinued-operations presentation are demonstrated, but the record does not establish which historical OE observations were taken from unrecast older filings. The current anchor is capped at latest OE, limiting the direct anchor effect, but a contaminated history could still influence the 0%, 4%, and 7% growth judgments.
audit_findings.action: Trace each annual OE numerator to its filing and rebuild 2016-2024 on a continuing-operations basis excluding Software Integrity, then reassess and rerun the growth scenarios if the reconstructed record changes the growth evidence.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain an unusually low and partly non-recurring tax burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $148.0 million tax benefit, equal to 14.8% of the $996.7 million anchor; if fully retained, approximately $2.20 billion of BASE operating PV or $10.37 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A discrete tax benefit retained in anchor OE is grown and capitalized as recurring earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Our effective tax rate for fiscal 2025 is 4.0%, which included $64.8 million of U.S. federal research tax credit benefit, $106.9 million of foreign derived intangible income (FDII) deduction benefit, and $148.0 million of tax benefit for the reduction in valuation allowance, of which $111.0 million relates to the full valuation allowance release against state research credits.
audit_findings.explanation: The 4.0% FY2025 tax rate and $148.0 million valuation-allowance benefit are filed facts, but whether the OE calculation removed them is unresolved. The latest nine-month FY2026 effective tax rate of 19.8% reinforces that FY2025 was not a normal tax year. The potential effect is material to the estimated value even though it would not close the gap to the $416.31 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $996.7 million anchor to the tax provision, explicitly remove the $148.0 million valuation-allowance release if still present, classify other credits and deductions as recurring or discrete, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A known post-year-end restructuring cash cost is absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Updated expected charges of $425-$500 million; $236.3 million recorded and $171.4 million paid through July 31, 2026; maximum $2.36 per share before discounting
audit_findings.mechanism: A finite restructuring cash claim should reduce the equity bridge or explicit forecast rather than recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Total charges under the 2026 Plan are expected to be in the range of $300.0 million and $350.0 million, and will consist primarily of severance costs, other one-time termination benefits and facility exit costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated, and the latest filing increased expected charges to $425-$500 million. Even treating the entire $500 million as an incremental equity deduction would reduce the $18.407 billion BASE equity value by 2.7% and value per share by at most $2.36, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged. Future savings should not be netted against the charge without evidence.
audit_findings.action: Add the verified remaining cash portion as a dated one-time forecast or bridge deduction, excluding amounts already paid or captured in later OE, and do not perpetuate the charge.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling treats unused ESPP authorization as an outstanding claim
audit_findings.magnitude: 14.7 million shares, 6.9% of the denominator; removing them raises BASE value from $86.90 to approximately $93.39 per share, or 7.5%
audit_findings.mechanism: Unused plan capacity inflates fully diluted shares and depresses per-share value without representing issued rights or recognizing purchase proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: As of October 31, 2025, 14.7 million shares of common stock were reserved for future issuance under the ESPP.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator-definition error because reserved authorization is not an outstanding equity claim. Its effect is conservative. The computed correction is meaningful but does not approach the $416.31 market price or reverse the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace the 14.7 million-share authorization with quantified outstanding ESPP purchase rights using an appropriate treasury-stock treatment, and retain the authorization only as a separately labeled ceiling sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Adding back all acquired-intangible amortization could strip a real replacement cost
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 acquired-intangible amortization was $504.383 million and nine-month FY2026 amortization was $1,210.292 million; economic replacement cost unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding amortization back to OE without a maintenance replacement charge can overstate sustainable OE and every discounted scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: The economic useful life was determined based on the technology cycle related to each developed technology, as well as the cash-flows over the forecast period.
audit_findings.explanation: Finite useful lives and substantial amortization are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish the amount added back in the $996.7 million anchor or the portion economically replaced by ordinary R&D, selling expense, retention spending, or acquisitions. Because the filed amortization is large relative to anchor OE, the unresolved replacement-cost assumption may be material, but its value effect cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile anchor OE to each amortization addback, separate developed technology, customer relationships, backlog, and trade names, estimate maintenance replacement spending from filed operating costs and acquisition history, and rerun scenarios with justified partial-addback sensitivities.
